summary: Head Harbour Light on Campobello Island, NB: an 1829 octagonal timber tower, a fog-signal story from 1875 to 1880, and volunteer care since 2000.

light.fog_signal: fog horn, blast 4 s, silence 56 s

structures.note: 51 feet; red cross painted on one side; larger lantern room placed on top in 1842
1 1/2 storey; heritage statement dates it c1840
class-C diaphone; heritage statement dates it 1914 to 1915

access.note: Reached on foot only at or near low tide; small fee to cross, run by the Friends.

visit.note: Friends run low-tide crossings and offer half-price tower tours to members; the 2026 season was to close 11 October.

events.note: Appropriation of £400 in February 1829; total cost £656
Light in operation the same year; John Snell first keeper
Gale broke the sea nearly halfway up the tower; keeper's boat and stores carried away
Keeper's dwelling built near the tower
Larger lantern room placed atop the tower; red cross painted on the eastern side
Steam Neptune fog trumpet; discontinued the following year
Improved steam fog signal, $6,199, in operation 30 January 1880
New iron lantern room with plate glass windows housing a third-order lens
Fog bell operated by machinery from 8 December 1904
Tower repaired; new tramway and bridge to the mainland
New fog alarm building with class-C diaphone
Wooden sea wall at the base replaced by concrete

Classified status by the Federal Heritage Building Review Office
Friends of the Head Harbour Lightstation formed and took over its care as a non-profit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Friends' history puts John Snell's tenure at about 1830 to the mid-1840s; LighthouseFriends' list has John B. Snell 1831 to 1861. The roster follows LighthouseFriends, which names the later keepers, and the disagreement is kept in the note.

The Friends' website and LighthouseFriends date the Friends' taking over of the station's care to 2000, when they became a non-profit. The heritage statement records a transfer of the lightstation to the Friends in 2006. The story gives both dates.
LighthouseFriends gives 1915 for the new fog alarm building with a class-C diaphone; the heritage statement dates the fog alarm building and work shed to 1914 to 1915. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: LighthouseFriends is copyrighted and facts-only: the story paraphrases it and keeps quotations to a few words. The 1830 Saint John Courier report, the Mary Snell memoir (its date is given in no source read, so the story gives none) and the 1875 Winchester letter are reached only through LighthouseFriends; none was read in the original. The Friends' history (1785 proposal by Giliam Butler, David Owen's 1829 deed) is an owner's account; the story uses only the deed, attributed to the Friends. Keeper dates disagree: LighthouseFriends lists John B. Snell 1831 to 1861 while its text and the Friends give about 1829 or 1830 for the first keeper; the Friends date his tenure to the mid-1840s. Henry McLaughlin (Head Harbour, 1872 to 1879) and Henry McLaughlin (Gannet Rock, 1843 to 1853) share a name; not linked. Douglas Daggett (1960 to 1971 here) and Douglas S. Daggett (Gannet Rock, 1971 to 1974) share a name; not linked. E. C. Dinsmore is not linked to Samuel G. Dinsmore at Big Duck Island in the Department's tables. The heritage statement records a 2006 transfer of the lightstation to the Friends, which the story sets against the Friends' 2000 date (see resolved_conflicts); the 1988 classified status is given by the statements, LighthouseFriends and the Friends. The record's own 2006 provincial designation is unchecked. The record's climbable: true conflicts with LighthouseFriends (tower closed) and the Friends' mention of tower tours; the story does not claim the tower is open to climb. The record's tower height 15.0 m is close to the 15.5 m (51 ft) in the heritage statement; the Coast Guard list gives 15.1 m structure height. The record's first_lit is empty; LighthouseFriends, the heritage statement and the Friends all give 1829. The Friends' own page says the 2026 season would close 11 October; that date is past as of this research, so the closure line should be checked against the Friends' site before publication. The Marine report tables for 1880s and 1890s are not in the corpus, so the 1877 and 1880 fog-signal dates rest on LighthouseFriends.
